item.title: Captures: MP list around a reply (#567), AQ refusals from a local instance (#574)
item.body:
Closes #567
Closes #574
Claim: mac/m2-lead

**Problem.** Two captures were owed: the MP list before and after a reply in an already-unread conversation (#567), and the refusal answers of the AQ create endpoint (#574), which must never be probed live.

**Cause.** Neither state was in the corpus; the AQ refusals need a local instance of the server, schema only. Those local files then had no position control: every kit gate looked for the AQ host, and a local meta names `192.0.2.1`.

**What changed.**
- New anonymized fixtures `R336`-`R338`, `W138`-`W140`, `T52`-`T71`, manifest runs 12 and 13, `docs/HFR-PROTOCOL.md` entries. Nothing in the engine or the app. AQ answers come from a local instance of `toyo@96c0aea`, no request reached the live service.
- `publish.py` keeps the capture `origin`, and for `origin: local-instance` also `response_headers` and, when no file holds the bytes, `body_length`, so `T62`, `T67` and `T68` show their status, headers and size. Only those fields changed in the 15 metas, the answers are byte-identical to the first publish.
- `anonymize.py`: `verify_aq_own` now covers `origin: local-instance` metas (`verify_aq_local_meta`: exact keys, fixed host and paths, closed values, `origin` itself), `verify_aq_local_answer` covers their answers, `publish.py`'s AQ gate covers them too.
- Two issues in one PR, against AGENTS.md §3.6: they were one capture batch and share the manifest and protocol lines. The operator decides whether that stands.

`Closes #567`: the two captures, the optional third reply and the row facts it lists are here. The group conversation it marks optional and the case of an older thread, which `R336`-`R338` cannot show, moved to #610. Other AQ states: #591 (addition past the flood limit), #611.

**Tests.** 330 kit tests pass, 75 script tests pass, `check --corpus` 549 of 549 clean, `check-lot-deps.py` and `markdownlint-cli2` 0 errors, `pre-commit run --all-files` passes. New:
- `test_aq_own.py`, `AQLocalTests`: a planted value per position (`test_a_real_value_in_the_request_body_fails`, `test_every_other_position_is_closed`, `test_response_headers_are_closed`, `test_a_planted_answer_fails`, `test_origin_cannot_be_another_value_or_dropped`, `test_a_local_mark_on_another_host_fails`, `test_corpus_check_applies_it_through_the_meta`).
- `test_publish.py`: `test_publish_keeps_status_headers_and_size_of_a_local_answer`, `test_publish_refuses_a_local_capture_with_a_planted_value`, `test_publish_refuses_a_local_capture_whose_headers_do_not_fit`.
- `HopResponseParserTests`: `W138`-`W140` join the success set.
Shown to fail without the change: with the gates removed, 9 of these tests fail.

Independent leak check (own harvest) at the first publish: one finding, a real login in an upstream citation, fixed by citing `toyo@96c0aea`. This round adds only the `response_headers` and `body_length` fields to the corpus.

## Adversarial review (Opus 5.5) at 5cc3319c074cb4c4ffd505efe7f46393db052fc5

**REQUEST CHANGES.** Read: FIXTURES, LESSONS, AGENTS §3, §5, §8, REVIEW-ROUNDS, the diff, `T52`-`T71`, `R336`-`R338`, `W138`-`W140` with their metas, and `aq/api/addAlerte.php` and the DAO at `toyo@96c0aea`. Run at this head: `check --corpus` 549 of 549 clean, plus mutations on copies. Leak harvesting out of scope. Swift tests not run here: at review time the two macOS jobs were still pending.

**Confirmed:** every row fact of `R336`-`R338` (icon, `sujetCase7`/`8`/`9`, `[non lu]`, row 1 of 50), `W138`-`W140`, the codes and lists of `T52`-`T61`, `T69`, `T71`, the `:69` and `:95` source citations. The `origin` field in `publish.py` and its test are fine.

### Findings

1. **Medium. `docs/HFR-PROTOCOL.md:680` (and the bold heading at `:679`): the conclusion handed to LOT-140 overclaims.** It says "the icon and the order do not change". Line 679 itself says the thread was already row 1, so these lists cannot show that. `R336`'s 50 rows are in descending last-post order, so a reply to an older thread would be expected to move it. Scenario: LOT-140 trusts order stability and misses or mis-tracks a reply on an older unread conversation, the case it exists for. Fix: heading "Row 1 stays row 1", drop "and the order" from `:680`, state the older-thread case as *pending capture* with an issue (#567 asked for the order).

2. **Medium. `docs/HFR-PROTOCOL.md:650`, `MANIFEST.md:102-106, 365-368`: facts no fixture shows, and the class of the last fixes was not closed.** Metas keep status and content type only, no header and no body size. `T62` has the same limits as `T67`/`T68`, but `:650` sits under "**verified**" and states "empty body" and `Content-Length: 0` with `T62` as its source. MANIFEST `T62`, `T67`, `T68` state `Content-Length` and "empty body" flatly (`T67`: "no `Content-Length`", while `:651` says the fixture does not keep that), run 13 speaks of the `Host` and `X-Powered-By` headers no fixture holds, and `T69` says "the three AQs were deleted" although it is one topic's list. Scenario: a LOT-055 test for the empty 200 has no bytes to read, and the spec reads as if it had. #574 asked for "status, headers and bytes", which the published files do not hold for these states. Fix: label them run observations in both files (the source backs the 403s at `addAlerte.php:60-61, 136-137`, cite it), or better, store body size and response headers for these three.

3. **Medium. `tooling/fixtures/anonymize.py:2854` and `publish.py` (`is_aq_host`): the local files have no position control, and `origin` proves nothing.** Both gates test the host `aq.super-h.fr`; a local meta names `192.0.2.1`. Reproduced on copies, `check --corpus` stays clean with: a real topic id, title and permalink in `T53`'s `request_body`; a free-text `commentaire`; non-alias alert and message ids in `T54`. Caught correctly: a pseudo in the body, a pseudo or title in the list, a loopback URL. The published values are all fake, so nothing leaks today, but the next local run has no net (LESSONS 33). The PR body calls this a gap "for the lots", yet it is a kit gap with no issue, and rule 3.8 forbids hidden state. Fix: a position check for `origin: local-instance` metas (exact fields, alias forms, fixed host, `origin` restricted to that value) in this PR, or at the least an issue linked from the PR.

4. **Medium. `docs/HFR-PROTOCOL.md:651, 654, 681`: uncaptured states without an issue.** `:651` says *pending capture* without citing #591, which exists. `:654` and `:681` are "Not captured" lists with no issue, and `Closes #567` drops the group conversation the issue listed as optional. Fix: cite #591; open or name an issue for the rest, or keep `Refs #567`.

5. **Low. `docs/HFR-PROTOCOL.md:682`: the clean-up is under the section's "**verified** once" but rests on nothing published** (the answer sentence and both lists afterwards). Label it a run observation. MANIFEST run 12 also says `W64`'s body only, the protocol says `W64`'s and `W65`'s.

6. **Low. PR body, AGENTS §8.** "The docs name no unpublished fixture" is false (`:651` names `T64`-`T66`). The older-AQ gap was removed by `76e7b8a5`. "Reduced to one commit" no longer describes the branch. The tests section names none of what was added (`HopResponseParserTests`, `test_publish`), and the `publish.py` change is not a "control". Two issues in one PR against rule 3.6: fine if the operator accepts it, but say so.

7. **Low. `MANIFEST.md:97`, `tooling/fixtures/corpus.json:269-275`: collision with #609.** Both PRs add "Run 12", and this one moves `R335e` below the new rows, next to the line #609 appends to. Whoever merges second renumbers. Restore `R335e`'s place.

No test is asked for beyond the control of finding 3.

## Adversarial review round 2 (Opus 5.5) at b635c320a29ce220a04f60fbac26bac5e2bbfa95

**REQUEST CHANGES.** Every round 1 finding is really fixed and no value leaks. Three small findings on the new control code, the first one a fix side effect. Head unmoved. Scope: `5cc3319c..b635c320`, with `docs/FIXTURES.md` read first. Run here: 327 kit tests, `check --corpus` 549 of 549, about 80 mutations on copies. Swift tests not run here: Linux is green, the macOS and app jobs were pending. No forum request.

### Findings

1. **Medium. `tooling/fixtures/anonymize.py:2963`: a malformed `date` crashes the verifier and prints the value.** Failing scenario: a local meta with `"date": "PLANTEDVALUE"`, with a list file. `verify_aq_local_meta` reports it, then `parsedate_to_datetime` raises `ValueError: Invalid date value or format "PLANTEDVALUE"`. `check --corpus` stops with a traceback holding the value and no summary line, and `publish.py` does the same on the raw (it catches `AnonymizeError` only). The kit's rule is the opposite (`anonymize.py:1757`: "Never the offending value… CI logs are public"; `publish.py` docstring: "never values"), and the remaining files are not checked. The open CodeRabbit thread on this line says the crash, not the value in the log. Fix: `try/except (TypeError, ValueError)` around it, returning a finding with no value, plus a test that asserts the value is not in the output.

2. **Low. `tooling/fixtures/publish.py:71`: a malformed headers file ends the whole batch.** A header line without `": "` (tested: a stray line, a blank line) raises an uncaught `ValueError` and stops the run with a traceback. It fails closed and prints no value, so nothing leaks. Fix: as the open CodeRabbit thread on this function says, raise `A.AnonymizeError` so the capture is refused by name.

3. **Low. `tooling/fixtures/anonymize.py:2958-2961`: an XML comment or processing instruction in a local list passes both gates.** `ElementTree` drops them, so `<!-- free text -->` inside or before `<alertes>` gives no finding. Reproduced: `check --corpus` stays clean and `publish.py` writes the file with the comment in it. Nothing does so today, and a local server does not emit comments, but `docs/FIXTURES.md:45` and `tooling/fixtures/README.md:82` say every position is closed. Fix: match the whole text against the run's shape, or refuse `<!--` and any `<?` after the prolog, with a test.

### Round 1 findings

| # | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 Overclaimed order | Fixed. Heading "Row 1 stays row 1", conclusion scoped to a conversation at the top, "Do not rely on the row's position", older thread pending on #610. No "order unchanged" left in `MANIFEST.md` |
| 2 Facts no fixture shows | Fixed, not reworded: the bytes are now in the metas. `T62` 403, `body_length` 0, `Content-Length: 0`; `T67` 200, 0, no `Content-Length`; `T68` 403, 0, `Content-Length: 0`. Source citations `:60-61`, `:69`, `:69-76`, `:95`, `:136-137` checked at `toyo@96c0aea`. `T69` read after `T68`, labelled |
| 3 No position control | Fixed, apart from finding 3 above. All the round 1 mutations now fail: real topic id, title and permalink in `request_body`, free-text `commentaire`, non-alias alert and message ids. So do `origin` dropped or changed, private flag, note, extra field, `body_length` bool, string, negative or mismatched |
| 4 States without an issue | Fixed: #591, #610, #611 exist and hold those states |
| 5 Clean-up | Fixed, run observation in both files, `W64` and `W65` |
| 6 PR body | Fixed |
| 7 Collision with #609 | Fixed: `R335e` back in place. Merge of both heads: `corpus.json`, `HFR-PROTOCOL.md`, kit auto-merge; only the expected `MANIFEST.md` run block conflicts. Merged tree: 333 kit tests, `check --corpus` 568 of 568 clean |

### Metas and headers

- **15 metas, `T52`-`T62`, `T67`-`T69`, `T71`:** only `response_headers` added, and `body_length` on `T62`, `T67`, `T68`. No other key changed.
- **Header values:** `Host` (`192.0.2.1:8574`), `Date`, `Connection: close`, `X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.12`, `Content-type`, and where the server sent them `Cache-Control`, `Pragma`, `Content-Length`. No cookie, session id, host name, local path or user name. Same keys as raw; only `Host` differs (the loopback address is replaced). The port and the PHP version are run details, harmless, and the protocol entry states the version family.
- **Answers:** the 12 files are byte-identical to `5cc3319c`; `git diff` touches only metas and `MANIFEST.md` under the corpus.
- **Planted header on raw copies, `T53` (file) and `T62` (meta only), 22 cases each:** `Set-Cookie` in three casings, `Server`, a debug path, values planted in `Host`, `X-Powered-By`, `Connection`; `origin` = `local-instance`, `live`, `local`, empty, null, number, list, or absent, on the local, AQ and forum hosts. Nothing with `origin` was published. The code **refuses the capture** rather than dropping the header, which is stricter and writes neither file. With no `origin` the headers file is never read, so it cannot be published.
- **`check --corpus` on the published metas** also fails on a planted header, whatever the origin. A `response_headers` key added by hand to a meta with no `origin` on another host passes, if its value is no session value: `publish.py` cannot produce that, so no finding.

### Upstream login

`git log -p` of the branch, commit messages and authors included, with my own search (lower-cased, punctuation removed, URL-decoded; also reversed, hex, base64, digit-for-letter): 0 hits, and none in the tree. 17 citations, all `toyo@96c0aea`. The meta `note` and `AQ_LOCAL_NOTE` also say `toyo/aq`, the repository folder, no owner. No GitHub owner other than `ezzz` appears. Operator config values: 0 hits on added lines.

### Notes, not blocking

- `Closes #567`: both captures, the third reply and the row facts are here, the optional group case is on #610. The order of the rows, which #567 lists, is answered only for row 1, and the older thread is on #610. The PR body says so.
- Two issues in one PR, against rule 3.6: accepted by the operator.
- Two CodeRabbit threads are open, the ones in findings 1 and 2: fixing those two findings closes them.

## Adversarial review round 3 (Opus 5.5) at 53021bc9b47113b876fed6c3eed5c48e682bd65b

**REQUEST CHANGES.** One finding: round 2 finding 3 is fixed for every case except one, and that case still publishes. It takes one word and one test line. Findings 1 and 2 are really fixed, nothing regressed. Head unmoved. Scope: `b635c320..53021bc9`. Run here on copies: 329 kit tests, `check --corpus` 549 of 549, 11 mutations, planted values through `check --corpus` and `publish.py`. No forum request.

### Finding

1. **Low. `tooling/fixtures/anonymize.py:2958`: a processing instruction whose name starts with `xml-` or `xml.` passes both gates.** The `\b` in `\A\s*<\?xml\b[^>]*\?>` also matches before `-` and `.`, so the strip takes `<?xml-note free text?>` for the prolog, and `ElementTree` then drops it. Failing scenario: a list that starts `<?xml-note PLANTEDVALUE free text?>` (no prolog before it; after a real prolog it is caught). `verify_aq_local_answer` returns nothing, `check --corpus` stays clean, and `publish.py` answers `ok T9`, rc 0, and writes the file with the text in it. Same claim as round 2: `docs/FIXTURES.md:45`, "any position". Fix: `\b` becomes `\s`, and add `<?xml-note free text?>` to `test_a_comment_or_an_instruction_in_a_list_fails`. Note the test plants before `<alertes>`, after the prolog, so it needs a case that replaces the prolog. Tried on a copy: the case is refused by name, `publish.py` writes nothing, all 329 tests pass, and every legitimate list below still passes.

### Round 2 findings

| # | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 Malformed date | Fixed. `"date": "PLANTEDVALUE"` on `T54`, alone and with the same value in the `Date` header: `check --corpus` rc 1, no traceback, value absent, the summary line printed. `publish.py`: rc 1, "NOT written", value absent. Also tried: null, empty, a number, 31 Feb, year 99999, huge hour, huge offset: all a finding, no crash. A date with trailing text passes this parser, and `date not a local value` in the meta gate refuses it |
| 2 Malformed header line | Fixed. A blank line plus a stray line holding a planted value: `T9:0:0: headers file holds a line that is not a header`, "NOT written", rc 1, value absent, caught per capture so the batch goes on |
| 3 Comment or instruction | Fixed apart from the finding above |

### Mutations

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Comment guard removed | Fails, 3 subtests |
| Guard `<!` only; guard `<?` only; prolog not stripped | Fails |
| Date `try` removed; `TypeError` only; returns no finding | Fails |
| Header guard removed | Fails |
| Guard's BOM strip removed | Survives |
| Header guard `any` for `all`; `":"` for `": "` | Survive |

The three survivors fail closed (a BOM list is refused; a mixed file raises the old `ValueError`, with no value printed), so they are test gaps, not defects.

### Comment regex

- **BOM before the prolog:** handled. A BOM list passes, and BOM plus comment or instruction is refused. Two BOMs also pass, harmless: both are stripped.
- **`>` in the prolog:** the strip does not match, so the prolog stays and the guard refuses it. That is fail-closed and no legitimate list has one.
